name: cosmos-collective-v2
description: Multi-spectrum astronomical data exploration platform with citizen science features - Version 2

paragraphs: Fly a 3D solar system, image an exoplanet through the Sun's own gravity, browse JWST's infrared sky, and map 2,700+ Kepler worlds. Every datum is real, sourced, and dated - drawn live from NASA, ESA, STScI, NOAA, and CSIRO.
The Solar System explorer - real orbital mechanics, speed control from real time to a year per second, top and side views, and a dive to the Sun.
features: Solar System - accurate orbital mechanics with a speed control from real time to a year per second, free, top and side camera views, and a dive to the Sun. Zoom out to see the Sun's place in the Milky Way.
Webb explorer - JWST observations browsable by category and instrument (NIRCam, MIRI, NIRSpec), with feature annotations, a Hubble comparison mode, and deep links into the Sky Map.

Kepler Exoplanets - a live NASA Exoplanet Archive query rendering the confirmed planets across Sky, Galaxy, and HR-diagram views. Opens on a genuinely weird world (Kepler-16b, the real Tatooine) with the full catalogue…

Sky Map - the entire celestial sphere via Aladin Lite, with a first-class spectrum switcher (CMB, mid-IR, near-IR, optical, UV, gamma) and a live RA/Dec/FoV readout. Search any object; JWST markers deep-link back to…
Satellites - active satellites drawn at their current positions around a 3D Earth, filterable by orbit class (LEO, MEO, GEO, HEO) and constellation, with a follow-the-ISS mode.
